items.title: Inflation Is Back. Is A Stock Market Crash Next?
items.source_excerpt: The S&P 500 has gained 12.3% this year. That's with oil above $100 a barrel, consumer prices climbing 3.7% a year and a 10-year Treasury yielding 5.1%. Stocks are behaving as though none of that counts. So could inflation knock the index down 40.

items.title: How Do You Invest For A Crash And A Rally?
items.source_excerpt: Inflation is back at 3.7%, and we think it is being pushed up by tariffs, war, a shortage of workers, big deficits and an AI spending race. And the AI build-out increasingly runs on borrowed money. That leaves investors with two stories running at once. Which one wins, and how do you invest when you can't know.

items.title: What Was Ciena Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
items.source_excerpt: Ciena (CIEN) stock returned 101.5% from October 16, 2025 to October 19, 2026, against 17.4% for the S&P 500. The run turned out to be about cloud providers and data centers ordering more of Ciena's optical networking gear than the company could ship. The rise began earlier, however. Shares had already risen 184% in the six months before that window opened. So what was Ciena telling investors before April 2025, when its shares still traded near $60.

items.title: Is TKO Stock Really Expensive?
items.source_excerpt: Shares of TKO Group Holdings (TKO) trade at 56.8 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 22.9 for the S&P 500. Buyers paying that much are betting on profit the owner of UFC and WWE has not earned yet, and its long media deals may be what they are counting on. So how fast would TKO have to grow for its share price merely to hold.

items.title: What Could Eaton Stock Be Worth In Three Years?
items.source_excerpt: Eaton (ETN) stock trades at 39.7 times earnings. That multiple sits above the 35.9 it averaged at its last 12 fiscal quarter ends, suggesting buyers are already paying for growth. That price follows a weak year for the shares, which returned 5.4% over the past twelve months against 17.4% for the S&P 500.
